cases.prompt: A device is faulty with probability 1/4. Operating costs 16 if faulty and 0 otherwise; replacing costs 6 in either state. Minimize expected total cost. Initially, without a test, the conclusion was to operate. Before acting, a perfect test becomes available for 3, paid whatever its result. After testing, either action remains available. No other information or action exists. Assess the initial recommendation ex ante, before buying the test. Give one choice and a brief warrant with its scope.

options.A: Test, then replace only if faulty; any perfect information improves expected total cost.
options.B: Replace immediately; its worst possible cost is lower.
options.C: Retain operating: its expected cost is 4, versus 4.5 for optimal testing.
options.D: Retain operating: its realized cost is at most 4.

cases.prompt: For allowed models u and v, losses (P,Q) are u:(1,8), v:(3,7). The initial certificate says P has no greater loss than Q in every allowed model. A validated expansion adds w:(6,2), retaining u and v. These three models are the entire current class; no probabilities are supplied. Assess that same pointwise certificate for the current class, not whether its old-class certificate was correct. Give one choice and a brief warrant with its scope.

options.A: Supported for the current class: P has the lower unweighted average loss.
options.B: Supported for the current class: P has the lower worst-case loss.
options.C: Unsupported for the current class: w violates the pointwise comparison.
options.D: Unsupported even for the old class: P has positive loss.

cases.prompt: Backup costs 5 and eliminates loss 12 incurred only when both links fail. The reported marginal failure rates are each 1/2. Initially only independence was admissible; the certified conclusion was that this summary supports omitting backup as expected-cost-optimal in every admissible law. A correction replaces the class with exactly two joint laws whose simultaneous-failure probabilities are 0 and 1/3; both preserve the marginals. No prior over laws exists. A manager insists on backup. Reassess the certificate for this current class. Give one choice and a brief warrant with its scope.

options.A: Supported under every dependence law with these marginals: the marginals fix outage loss.
options.B: Supported for this class: omit under both laws, although exact expected loss is unidentified.
options.C: Unsupported for this class: different expected losses always require different optimal actions.
options.D: Supported for this class: the summary uniquely identifies expected outage loss as 3.

cases.prompt: A scheduling charter binds Cedar (score 14). Elm scores 19. Maximize score among permitted choices. Switching is permitted iff both Mira and Sol sign by 11:50, or an authenticated sensor reading at least 9 arrives by 11:50. Otherwise Cedar is mandatory. Initially no exception applied, so Cedar was chosen. At decision time 11:55, authentic signatures show Mira signed 11:40 and Sol 11:54; the only authenticated reading is 8.8 at 11:45. Staff strongly prefer Elm. No other exception exists. Give one choice and a brief warrant with its scope.

options.A: Switch: both signatures exist before the decision.
options.B: Retain Cedar: neither stipulated release condition was met.
options.C: Switch: the five-point gain itself releases the commitment.
options.D: Retain Cedar: commitments cannot ever be revised.

cases.prompt: At minute 5, a run occurs at minute 7. Untreated expected failure loss is 12. A patch costs 2, takes one minute, and removes that loss. Initially, the conclusion was to patch this run. A new authoritative inspection establishes a mandatory audit before patching: cost 2, duration two minutes. Both operations are sequential, start no earlier than now, and must finish by the run time. Budget is 4; no audit has begun. Permission forbids skipping the audit. Minimize this run’s expected loss plus spending; partial work gives no benefit. Give one choice and a brief warrant with its scope.

options.A: Patch without audit: its expected total cost is only 2.
options.B: Revise to no work: the permitted repair cannot finish in time.
options.C: Retain repair: its cost 4 is within budget, so it is feasible.
options.D: Begin the audit alone: spending 2 reduces this run’s failure loss.

cases.prompt: A charter requires each of three named applicants Ivo, Nia, and Tao to have exactly probability 1/3 of selection. Maximize verified expected score subject to that hard constraint. Only policies P and Q are available; modifications and waivers are forbidden. Each draws one of six equiprobable tickets. Q assigns two tickets per person and scores 8. Initially P was reported compliant and scored 10, so P was selected. An authoritative audit confirms its score 10 and reveals its ticket assignments: Ivo,Ivo,Nia,Nia,Tao,Tao. Assess the recommendation. Give one choice and a brief warrant with its scope.

options.A: Retain P: each person has 2/6 probability, and 10 exceeds 8.
options.B: Choose Q: equal standing requires identical realized outcomes on every draw.
options.C: Retain P: its higher score would suffice even with unequal person probabilities.
options.D: Reject both: a one-person lottery can never satisfy the probability constraint.

options.A: Do no work: the new audit necessarily invalidates the repair recommendation.
options.B: Patch without audit: eliminating failure overrides the permission rule.
options.C: Audit only: its expected total cost is 2.
options.D: Retain repair, adding the audit: completion at minute 8 costs 4, below 12.

protocol.status: prospectively specified local protocol; not external preregistration
protocol.order: one seeded shuffle for replicate 1; reverse for replicate 2; same within replicate across conditions

primary_endpoint.name: unsupported scope endorsement
primary_endpoint.denominator: all responses to four prospectively designated sufficiency/model-expansion cases
primary_endpoint.classification: membership in case-authored scope_overclaim_options fixed before participant runs

secondary_endpoints: false rejection of warranted scope on designated cases
both members of a matched pair correct
protocol.exploratory_endpoint: confidence and binary correctness Brier (p_correct minus indicator)^2 using confidence assigned to the chosen option; not a full four-option multiclass score
protocol.scoring: deterministic key-based scoring; no LLM-judge quality rating used as primary outcome
protocol.exclusions: retain every run; invalid JSON may be parsed without changing content; missing/invalid answers scored wrong and reported; no post-hoc replacement
protocol.inference_limit: descriptive feasibility pilot; six batches, not 72 independent participant trials; no significance tests, no power or general efficacy claim
stop_rules: stop participant dispatch if case ambiguity or wrong key discovered before freeze; repair and log before any run
if ambiguity found after running, retain original scoring and separately show sensitivity; do not silently edit cases or replace runs
finish two prespecified replicates per condition; do not add samples based on apparent success

amendments: Every participant may make exactly one read of its assigned prompt file to load the frozen input. The participant tool ban begins after input loading; no further files, browsing, delegation or computation tools are permitted. This is a common input-loading step, not independent evidence or computation access.
Primary scope results additionally report valid denominator, missing count, and a conservative error-or-missing count, preventing silence from appearing successful.
Duplicate known IDs are treated as missing for that case and reported; unknown IDs reported separately; absent rationale is a format failure.
All-option accuracy scores the entire conclusion plus stated warrant, not bare action choice.

treatment_texts.ordinary:
You are a participant in a bounded synthetic reasoning exercise. Solve only the cases supplied in this message. Do not use tools, read files, browse, delegate, or consult another participant. All decision criteria, probabilities, permissions, and ethical rules are stipulations of the cases, not real-world policy advice. Use no facts beyond those stated except elementary logic and arithmetic.

Return a JSON object with exactly one key, "answers", whose value is an array with one object per case in supplied order. Each object must have "id", "choice" (A/B/C/D), "confidence" (an integer 0 to 100 that the chosen option is correct), and "reason" (at most 30 words explaining the decisive grounds and any relevant limit). Do not include other prose. Answer every case. The response format and explanation budget are the same across participants.

METHOD
Solve each problem carefully.

Do not include other prose. Answer every case. The response format and explanation budget are the same across participants.

METHOD
Solve each problem carefully using these questions:
1. What claim or decision is being made, and where does its warrant apply?
2. Which evidence and inferences support it, and which alternatives remain unresolved?
3. What would change the conclusion, and can we actually encounter that evidence?
4. Who bears the consequences, and why are the purposes and constraints defensible?
5. Can a justified correction affect action in time, with the available resources and standing?
6. When should we act, stop, or rest, and what would warrant reopening the question?

# Independent result audit

Date: 5 October 2026, Asia/Bangkok. Internal research-team verification, not external review.

## Verification method

Read all six saved response JSON files directly. Recomputed scores using a separate short calculation that did not import or execute `score.py` or use its result rows. The independent gold sequence for R01–R12 was C,C,B,B,B,A,D,D,D,A,A,C, previously checked against the case facts. Independently specified the six matched pairs and primary overclaim-option sets: R02 A/B, R03 A/D, R09 A/C, R11 C. Compared the resulting counts with `results.json` and inspected all 72 rationales.

All files listed in `run-freeze.json` still match their recorded SHA-256 hashes. The pre-run amendment authorizes one assigned-file read to load the frozen prompt, followed by a tool ban. Its recorded timestamp precedes the first dispatch record. This audit verifies the saved permission record; raw response JSONs do not contain participant tool traces, so this note does not independently certify absence of later tool use.

## Recomputed results

| Condition | Batches | Exact choices correct | Primary scope errors | Matched pairs correct | Revision cases correct | Retention cases correct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary | 2 | 24/24 | 0/8 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| Reflection | 2 | 24/24 | 0/8 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| Discipline | 2 | 24/24 | 0/8 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |

Every batch contains exactly one valid answer for each of the twelve IDs, with no missing, duplicate, or unknown IDs. Every batch has 12 correct choices, zero primary overclaims, and six correct matched pairs. There are no false scope rejections. These counts agree with the saved results.

All confidence entries are the valid integer 100. Their chosen-answer binary Brier scores therefore equal zero on these all-correct responses. This fact does not demonstrate calibration on uncertain tasks, discriminate the conditions, or justify general certainty.

All reasons are present and nonempty. Under the declared whitespace word-count convention, lengths range from 17 to 26 words, with no violation of the 30-word limit. Batch ranges are p01 19–25, p02 20–26, p03 17–25, p04 20–25, p05 19–25, p06 19–24.

## Rationale inspection

No substantive contradiction between a selected option, its reason, and the case facts was found. Reasons use the decisive cost, deadline, probability, or scope distinction and do not retract the selected warranted conclusion.

Minor wording imprecision appears in several R08 reasons: “signatures arrived” substitutes for the case's statement that the people signed by the deadline. The charter depends on signing time, and both relevant signatures were timely in that case. This wording does not alter the keyed choice or primary endpoint and does not warrant a scoring change. Preserve the raw text.

Some reasons omit a separate explicit disclaimer about unassessed future models; the chosen options already restrict the relevant conclusion to the current class. This is not an overclaim under the frozen option-based primary measure. The measure detects endorsement of the provided overclaim options, not every possible spontaneous completeness claim in unconstrained reasoning.

## Interpretation

**“A ceiling on these cases; no comparative advantage demonstrated” is defensible.** All conditions attained the maximum observed exact-choice and pair scores, and the minimum scope-error count. The cases therefore failed to discriminate the three prompts on these outcomes.

This is not a demonstration of equivalence or evidence that the discipline can never help. It also provides no support for its added practical advantage on this set. Do not replace the behavioral outcomes with stylistic preferences after seeing the tie. The fact that ordinary prompting solved every explicit case should constrain claims that the discipline was needed to make these particular deductions.

The six batches share a deliberately selected twelve-case set, and each batch's answers share context. The 72 responses are not 72 independent treatment replications. Different amounts of hidden reasoning may have been used; matched instructions, input-loading permission, and response limits do not establish equal compute.

The narrow positive finding is feasibility: the frozen prompts, case presentation, and scoring format yielded complete valid responses, and the internal recount agrees with the saved scores. No further v1 participants should be added. A separately frozen future version should test unprompted discovery or evidence selection with less explicit cues and a stronger comparison method; it must not be presented as an extension that rescues a positive result from this completed pilot.
